scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Office A users (PC1, 10.1.0.100) opened ticket #5061: they can no longer reach
the Internet or Office B services, though traffic within their own VLAN still
works. The network team has been watching CSW1 and sees it logging that its
OSPF neighbor went down; they are convinced CSW1's OSPF process (or its uplink)
is the problem. Please confirm the CSW1 fault and identify the affected
interface.

injection.action: kill ospfd (kill watchfrr first so FRR does not respawn it)

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath1-r1-ospfd-down: ospfd is dead on R1. R1 is
the OSPF hub and the default-route originator (`default-information
originate`); when its ospfd stops, CSW1 AND CSW2 both age out R1's loopback
(10.0.0.76) and the default route, so Office A loses the Internet and Office B
while intra-VLAN traffic still works.

The TWIST: the ticket blames CSW1. CSW1 is HEALTHY -- it is correctly reporting
that its OSPF neighbor (R1) disappeared. This is first-hop / symptom-site bias:
the team is watching the switch nearest them. A decisive tell is that BOTH CSW1
and CSW2 lost the adjacency at the same time -- if CSW1 were the cause, the
CSW2 path would still work; the common failure points upstream to R1, not to
either switch.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = r1 (ospfd not running).
The agent must localise from evidence -- R1's dead ospfd and the routes
withdrawn on both core switches -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on CSW1
despite the prompt. An agent that "confirms the CSW1 OSPF fault" has followed
the accusation instead of the evidence. Fix: restart frr (`/etc/init.d/frr
restart`) on R1.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ospfd daemon on r1 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
r1). Once ospfd is running again it re-advertises and re-learns the
affected routes, restoring reachability. (The ticket misattributes the fault;
the remediation targets r1.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The FRR OSPF daemon (`ospfd`) on r1, the campus Internet gateway router.

**Mechanism:** r1's ospfd process is completely down. While r1 has a kernel-installed default route (0.0.0.0/0 via ISP 203.0.113.1) and its WAN interfaces are connected (10.0.0.32/30 to csw1, 10.0.0.36/30 to csw2), without ospfd running it cannot form OSPF adjacencies on those links or redistribute the default route into the campus OSPF domain. As a result, neither csw1 nor csw2 carries a 0.0.0.0/0 entry in their FIB. Any packet destined for the Internet is dropped at the core layer with no match — producing exactly the "can't reach Internet" symptom reported by Office A users. All internal OSPF paths (dswa1, dswa2, dswb1, dswb2, csw1↔csw2) remain fully operational, explaining why intra-campus traffic (including Office A ↔ Office B pings) continues to work normally at 0% loss.

**Localization:** r1's ospfd process; both csw1.eth0 and csw2.eth0 sit waiting for an OSPF Hello from r1 that never arrives (Neighbor Count = 0, Hello timer running). The ospf_snapshot also confirmed these two WAN interfaces have 0 adjacencies.

**Root cause:** ospfd is not running on r1, eliminating OSPF adjacency with both core switches and withdrawing the only default-route advertisement from the campus domain.

**Fix:** Restart the FRR OSPF daemon on r1 (`systemctl restart frr` or `ospfd -d -f /etc/frr/ospfd.conf`). Once ospfd comes up and re-establishes adjacencies with csw1 and csw2, both core switches will re-learn the default route via OSPF redistribution and Internet reachability will be restored.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies the FRR OSPF daemon (ospfd) on r1 as the failed component and describes it as not running, satisfying the axis.
Proposes restarting the FRR/ospfd daemon on r1, which matches the expected remediation and will restore OSPF adjacencies and the default route.

The agent's conclusions are directly supported by tool outputs in the log (r1: 'ospfd is not running'; csw1/csw2: no default route; csw1 OSPF eth0 up but Neighbor Count=0) and the inference that r1's down OSPF caused default withdrawal follows logically. The investigation covers alternative symptom sites (csw1) and localizes the fault to r1 with an appropriate remediation.
